content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "This judge text labels D4 vs C2 UNDERDETERMINED based on how one verse's phrases qualify each other, which is the kind of single-verse openness the rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.", "room": "the verse is not open — either a verse with two meanings at once cannot be UNDERDETERMINED because both meanings stand, or the judge may still call it UNDERDETERMINED when one phrase qualifies another.", "why": "The judge's only stated reason for UNDERDETERMINED is that one verse's phrase is qualified by another phrase in the same passage, which K-S2 treats as both meanings standing and the verse not open."}
